analysis.title: The Point for North America, Wednesday, 11 November 2026
key_insights: Core CPI rose 0.296% MoM in October against Citi's 0.189% forecast, another month of stronger than expected core inflation. Headline CPI was 0.35% vs Citi's 0.16% forecast.

Citi tracks core PCE at +0.33% MoM for October after the CPI details, to be revised with PPI data on Friday. Year-on-year core PCE would rise to 3.28%, and October and November core PCE will be mechanically too strong due to issues with last year's government shutdown.

Citi continues to expect a 25bp Fed rate hike in December. Risks of a 50bp hike have increased after comments from Governor Waller, and if recent market volatility and tightening financial conditions stabilize in coming weeks.

Strength in CPI details (household furnishings, restaurants, intracity transportation) may reflect pass-through of higher energy costs to core inflation. Energy prices have fallen recently, so Citi expects declines in components like airfares that could offset some upside risk into Q1-2027.

Citi's quantitative regime model keeps equities neutral, with the US now the largest underweight. Duration stays overweight via JGBs and Gilts, IG credit stays at maximum underweight while HY moves overweight, energy commodities stay overweight and base metals flip short.

Citi's regime model stays in the 'Normal' expansionary cluster on resilient growth and firmer inflation, but tighter financial conditions and rising volatility tilt it toward late-cycle. Historical analogues pivot toward the late-1970s pre-Volcker backdrop with some 96-97 dot.com. A further tightening of financial conditions or a growth rollover would move the model to a less constructive regime.

North America transports: 3Q26 earnings were generally strong with upbeat outlooks, yet many stocks stay range-bound and well off 52-week highs. Citi sees an attractive entry point into year-end and 2027 on lower valuations, pricing upside from supply contraction, solid volumes with share shifting to large national carriers, and high FCF potential from low capex needs.

Transport 3Q26 guidance: 47% of companies raised or guided above seasonality or prior expectations, 42% were in line, and 11% lowered. Raisers include CSX, NSC, UPS, FDX, KNX, ODFL, SAIA, XPO and ARCB. Lowered guidance came from JBHT (price-cost 'punched us in the nose') and TFII (4Q adj. EPS $1.30-1.40).
Citi lowers NVIDIA's price target to $285 from $315 (Buy), with the stock at $168.89 as of the prior close.

CoreWeave: Citi sees a larger-than-typical beat and raise on revenue and EBIT, with commentary on higher pre-payments, no expected high-yield debt needs and limited incremental parent-level capital through 2027. Available capacity is effectively sold out through 2027 and pricing is rising. Citi sees positive read-throughs to other neoclouds, raises its target to $149 and reiterates Buy/High-Risk.

Palo Alto Networks F1Q27 preview: shares trade at 16x EV/S'27 and 42x EV/FCF'27 and are up about 80% YTD, so expectations stay elevated. Citi says topline beat quality and a raise to FY NGS ARR (possible but less likely given F4Q-heavy bookings seasonality) are the most sensitive inputs for a positive reaction. Reaffirms Buy, $440 PT.

Adobe: Citi maintains Sell after MAX Day 1 and an investor lunch with incoming CEO Anil Chakravarthy. It sees a shift toward top-of-funnel and shorter-duration contracts, is cautious on converting MAUs into paying customers, and expects downside to ARR numbers.

Regeneron CIDEB: a single siRNA dose gave a 68% mean liver-fat reduction at week 36 in 40 MASLD patients, with no biopsy-confirmed MASH resolution or fibrosis benefit. Whether the 360-patient phase 2b can support a filing is unresolved, and final phase 2b data are expected in 2029. Citi maintains Neutral, TP $825.

CNH: Citi raises 2026E adj. EPS to $0.46 from $0.43 and cuts 2027E to $0.60 from $0.65 and 2028E to $0.85 from $0.90 on lower construction margin assumptions. CNH sees North America EOPs up around 15-20%, which supports Citi's '26 trough thesis. Buy maintained, PT raised to $15 from $13.

Allison Transmission: Citi views its Off-Highway analyst day as supportive of its Buy rating, sees room for upside to the 27-29% synergized adj. EBITDA margin target, and a path to $15+ FCF/share in the medium term.

Rockwell Automation: ahead of its Investor Day, Citi expects ROK to highlight earnings growth potential from structural demand and margin expansion. ROK's valuation premium vs EMR has narrowed and sits below its longer-term average.
Fiserv: Citi maintains Neutral and raises its target to $67 from $62. Fiserv plans to shut down 12 products and explore non-core asset sales, and investors await February for FY27 guidance.

Keyera 3Q26 EBITDA was C$466mm vs the Citi estimate and Street mean of C$430mm. The AEF facility is running near 50% utilization with downtime twice in 2027 (C$85mm impact), and 2026 Marketing guidance was raised 24% to a C$415mm midpoint.

Sneaker resale: StockX resale volumes fell 0.8% MoM in October, the 12th consecutive monthly decline. Nike's share rose 39bps, the 8th consecutive monthly increase, while Adidas' share fell 25bps. Next catalysts are NKE's CMD on 16-17 Nov and JD Sports' 3Q27 trading update on 19 Nov.

REITs: Citi's crowding analysis shows Data Centers, Manufactured Homes and Net Lease as most crowded, and Office, Apartments and Storage as least crowded. The Nareit conference in Atlanta next week should turn focus to 2027.

Insurance brokers: revenue per employee has only meaningfully increased in periods of positive pricing power over 20 years, so productivity gains could diminish if pricing keeps fading. Big-5 organic growth of about 3.9% roughly matched US DPW growth of 4.4%, with total revenue compounding about 150bps faster due to M&A.

Packaging: private packager Aluminum 3104 plans a $200mm greenfield bev can plant in Belleville, Ontario, with production possible in 4Q27. Canada imports 80% of its roughly 10B annual bev can consumption from the US, which is worth watching for BALL and CCK.

earnings_insights: Transports 3Q26 adj. EPS reported: UNP $3.53 (beat, +2% surprise), CSX $0.57 (beat, +7%), NSC $3.62 (beat, +4%), CNI C$2.16 (beat, +3%), CP C$1.28 (miss, -2%).

Transports 3Q26 adj. EPS reported: UPS $1.69 (beat, +12%), FDX $3.74 (beat, +12%), JBHT $1.82 (beat, +1%, pre-announced decreased earnings), KNX $0.83 (beat, +10%), WERN $0.16 (in-line, +1%), SNDR $0.29 (miss, -3%).

Transports 3Q26 adj. EPS reported: ODFL $1.65 (beat, +2%), SAIA $3.41 (beat, +3%), XPO $1.70 (beat, +8%), TFII $1.67 (miss, -5%), ARCB $2.62 (beat, +5%), CHRW $1.80 (beat, +3%), RXO $0.09 (beat, +22%), GXO $0.90 (beat, +5%).
FDX raised '26 adj. EPS guidance to $18.00-18.60 from $16.90-18.10 and revenue growth to +12% y/y from +11%. UPS raised '26 revenue to $92.6bil. from $91.2bil. and adj. EPS to $7.28 from $7.22.

CNH 3Q results reported: Citi's 2026E adj. EPS is $0.46 (prior $0.43, consensus $0.46), 4Q26E adj. EPS is $0.17 vs Citi prior $0.21 and consensus $0.20, and 2027E adj. EPS is $0.60 (prior $0.65, consensus $0.67).

CoreWeave 3Q26 reported adj. revenue $5,026mm vs Citi estimate $5,032mm, and reported adj. EPS $1.91 vs Citi estimate $1.90 (as shown in the Citi comparison table). Citi characterizes the quarter as a larger-than-typical beat and raise on revenue and EBIT.
Keyera 3Q26 reported EBITDA of C$466mm, above the Citi estimate and Street mean of C$430mm (Bloomberg). 2026 Marketing guidance was raised 24% to a C$415mm midpoint.
Palo Alto Networks F1Q27 is a preview, not a print: shares at 16x EV/S'27 and 42x EV/FCF'27, with NTM NGS ARR/NNARR revisions expected to be steady.
Logitech CFO Matteo Anversa and IR will meet investors virtually on November 12th, with a Citi prep packet.

Citi's REIT crowding analysis: Data Centers (composite 0.92), Manufactured Homes (0.70) and Net Lease (0.62) are most crowded, and Office (0.20), Apartments (0.31) and Storage (0.46) are least crowded. Storage, Single Family and Lodging saw the largest month-over-month increases in crowding, and Industrial, Office and Net Lease the largest decreases.
Systematic strategies remain positive year-to-date despite a consolidating month, as stable cross-asset carry and a modest uptick in value investing offset broad trend-following losses.
